description:
As part of your penetration testing assignment, you have scanned a target network and obtained a list of open ports for multiple hosts, saved in the file /home/user/scan_results.txt. Each line of this file contains an IP address, followed by a space, and then an open port number (e.g., "192.168.1.10 22"). 

Your goal is to identify which ports are most commonly open across all the hosts. 

To do this:

1. Process the file /home/user/scan_results.txt to count how many times each port appears (i.e., how many hosts have each port open).
2. Sort the results by port number in ascending order. 
3. For each port, output a line containing the port number, a space, then the count (e.g., "22 5").
4. Write the final output, with one port per line in this format, to the file /home/user/open_ports_frequencies.txt.

For verification, the /home/user/open_ports_frequencies.txt file will be checked to ensure it contains the correct port frequencies in the correct format and order. Be careful with spaces and the sorting order to exactly match the specified output format.
truth:
Before the task starts, the file /home/user/scan_results.txt exists with the following contents:
192.168.1.10 22
192.168.1.12 80
192.168.1.15 22
192.168.1.18 443
192.168.1.20 80
192.168.1.21 443
192.168.1.22 8080
192.168.1.23 22
192.168.1.30 80

After successful completion, the file /home/user/open_ports_frequencies.txt should exist and contain exactly:
22 3
80 3
443 2
8080 1
